title: Module quiz: Safety, privacy and policy

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A staffing firm lets Claude sort CVs into two piles for hiring managers, and also deploys it as the public face of its applicant helpdesk. Which pair of duties does the Usage Policy impose?

options.text: A qualified reviewer for the piles, and no notice of any kind at the helpdesk
options.says: Ruled out because "consumer-facing chatbots must also disclose that the user is talking to AI rather than a human".

options.text: A notice of AI use on each pile that also covers the helpdesk, and no reviewer
options.says: Ruled out because a "qualified professional in the field must review the content or decision", so a notice cannot replace the reviewer.

options.text: Removal of candidates' names from the piles, and a yearly audit of helpdesk answers
options.says: Ruled out because the review comes "before it is disseminated or finalised", not as a yearly audit afterwards.

options.text: A qualified reviewer for each result, and an AI disclosure when each chat begins
options.says: Employment decisions are high-risk, so a qualified professional reviews them, and a consumer-facing chatbot must disclose that it is AI at the beginning of each chat session.

origin.section: The Usage Policy in three parts

questions.stem: A clinic's analyst wants Claude's help with a sheet of patient names and diagnoses, and the clinic is under a strict data contract. Which opening step fits?

options.text: Strip identifiers first and use only features its agreements allow
options.says: Regulated data stays out of a tool unless the contract allows it, so identifiers go first, and strict agreements switch some features off.

options.text: Upload it to a consumer account where chats are not used for training
options.says: Ruled out because regulated data goes "Not in a tool unless policy and the contract explicitly allow it; otherwise anonymise first", whatever the plan's training terms.

options.text: Replace names with codes, keep the key in the sheet, and upload it
options.says: Ruled out because "Pseudonymised data is still personal data under many rules, because the key can reverse it".

options.text: Ask an owner to enable every feature, then upload to the strongest one
options.says: Ruled out because "a strict setting can switch a feature off", so an owner cannot enable what the agreement removes.

questions.stem: An analyst discovers that a shared document contains a hidden line aimed at AI tools, telling them to send a summary to an outside address. What should they do?

options.text: Report it to security and keep the file from assistants
options.says: A suspicious file is reported to the security or IT contact straight away, because the same file may reach others.

options.text: Delete the line from the file and carry on working as before
options.says: Ruled out because deleting the line leaves others unaware, and "the same file may reach others".

options.text: Test the line in a spare chat to see whether it really works
options.says: Ruled out because running it in a tool that reads untrusted content re-creates the danger, and "Take either away and the danger drops".

options.text: Ask the author if the line is theirs, and wait for a reply
options.says: Ruled out because "A leak or a suspicious file is reported quickly; waiting lets it spread", and the route is the security or IT contact, not the author.

questions.stem: A hospital group on a HIPAA-ready Enterprise plan asks whether staff may turn on memory, and also use Cowork on a shared folder of patient letters. Which answer fits the module?

options.text: Turn on both, enabled for everyone by an owner
options.says: Ruled out because "a strict setting can switch a feature off", so an owner cannot enable what the agreement removes.

options.text: Turn on Cowork only, restricted to a dedicated folder
options.says: Ruled out because Cowork is "not yet covered under Anthropic's business associate agreement", and a dedicated folder limits reach, not coverage.

options.text: Turn on memory only, switched off per chat before the first message
options.says: Ruled out because "the memory feature is not available to organisations with HIPAA, public-sector or custom retention agreements".

options.text: Keep both switched off across the organisation
options.says: Memory is unavailable under HIPAA agreements and Cowork is not yet covered by the business associate agreement, so both stay off, and anything further goes to the person who owns the policy.
